thread:
maya: Import run failing intermittently during HF->Redwood convert — safetensors shard reads hit 'Unexpected EOF' and converter aborts.

aj: Seen this pattern before. Any chance the hub is serving ranged responses and our downloader is not retrying ranges?

maya: Log snippet:
```
ERROR convert: safetensors shard read failed: unexpected EOF reading bytes (expected 1048576 got 81324)
  at downloader.fetch_range()
  http://huggingface.co/..., range: bytes=0-1048575, status=206
```

liu: Also noticed a separate failure where tokenizer special tokens vanish after convert. The HF `tokenizer.json` had an `added_tokens` entry with raw bytes (weird SFT): `{"id":50257,"content":"\\xff"}` — converter chokes on non-utf8 token content and silently drops it.

sam: On my quant experiments I hit a quality regression that looks like an off-by-one in position ids. config.json had `max_position_embeddings: 2048` but tokenizer.json implied 2049 (legacy +EOS). The convert path seems to pick from the wrong source when `rotary` attrs present.

import-bot: convert-job #8472 FAILED (exit 1) 

aj: Repro command I used: `redwood-hf-convert --model-id user/sft-example --revision v3 --out /tmp/conv --verbose` — when the hub responds with a 302 -> S3 signed URL our code was letting curl/requests follow redirects but NOT honoring the original `range` semantics, resulting in truncated shard reads.

maya: Also found a weight-key rename bug: keys like `base_model.model.decoder.lm_head.weight` end up renamed to `lm_head.weight` but we accidentally drop `decoder.` sometimes, causing tie/unify mismatch at load (tied embeddings not re-wired).

liu: Minimal workaround so far: 1) pre-normalize tokenizer.json to remove non-utf8 added tokens, 2) force full shard download (no range) for affected models, 3) pin revision with `--disable-redirects` so we can auth the S3 URL before range requests. Not great for large models.

sam: Did a quick local patch to retry partial reads when `Content-Range`/206 responses are smaller than requested — that reduced EOFs but still leaves tokenizer/weight-rename issues.

maya: Filing GH issue: redwood/convert#459 with logs and tiny repro shard + tokenizer.json. Linking here for context: https://github.com/redwood/convert/issues/459

aj: Quick checklist for the converter patch: - canonicalize tokenizer sources (tokenizer.json > tokenizer_config.json > config) for special tokens, and normalize byte tokens into escaped unicode; - when following redirects to storage, preserve range headers or switch to non-range full download fallback; - make key-rename idempotent and respect known prefixes (`base_model.`, `model.`) in ordered fashion so we don't double-strip.

maya: Thanks — I'll attach failing shard and tokenizer to the issue. If someone can help prototype the range-retry + full-download fallback that would be huge. :pray: 

aj: I can take the range/retry patch today. sam, can you look at the key-rename idempotency?

sam: Yep, will add unit tests for tied-weight detection.

maya: tagging @eng-oncall in case this hits any scheduled imports tomorrow.
